channel.title: Subaru recalls — Car Recall Tracker
channel.description: NHTSA vehicle safety recalls explained in plain English.

item.title: Subaru Ascent and Forester have wrong weight rating label
item.description: Subaru is recalling certain Crosstrek Hybrid, Forester, Forester Hybrid and Ascent vehicles. The certification label on these vehicles shows an incorrect Gross Axle Weight Rating, the maximum weight an axle is rated to carry. Because of this, the vehicles do not meet a federal safety standard covering tire and rim selection. Subaru will mail owners a new label free of charge, and owners who prefer can have a dealer install the new label instead, also free.

item.title: Toyota, Lexus and Subaru rearview camera may freeze
item.description: Toyota is recalling certain 2022 through 2026 Toyota and Lexus vehicles and the Subaru Solterra that have the Panoramic View Monitor camera system. Models include RAV4, Highlander, Prius, Sienna Hybrid, Camry Hybrid, Mirai, bZ4X and the Lexus NX and TX Hybrid. A software error can cause the backup camera picture to freeze or go blank when the car is in reverse, so these vehicles do not meet the federal rear visibility standard.

item.title: Toyota bZ4X and Subaru Solterra Defroster May Fail
item.description: On some bZ4X and Solterra electric vehicles, certain HVAC system faults, such as the electric compressor failing, can cause the windshield defroster and defogger system to stop working. This can happen under certain driving conditions.

item.title: Subaru Forester Child Seat Anchor Bolts May Loosen
item.description: Some Subaru Forester vehicles have bolts that anchor a child seat in place, and these bolts may not have been tightened properly at the factory when the vehicle was built. Because of this, the bolts can come loose over time. A loose anchor bolt means the hardware used to attach a child seat to the vehicle may not hold it as firmly in place as it should.

item.title: Subaru Forester Alloy Wheels May Be Improperly Attached
item.description: Some 2025 Subaru Forester vehicles with 18-inch aluminum alloy wheels may have wheels made with an incorrectly specified lug seat surface. This can result in a wheel not being properly attached to the vehicle. An improperly attached wheel can cause the vehicle to lose stability while being driven. This loss of stability can make the vehicle harder to control on the road.

item.title: Subaru Legacy, Outback Passenger Air Bag May Not Deploy
item.description: A capacitor inside the sensor that detects whether the front passenger seat is occupied may crack and short circuit. If this happens, the front passenger air bag may not deploy in a crash.

item.title: Subaru Outback, Forester switch failure disables reverse lights, camera
item.description: Subaru is recalling certain Crosstrek, Forester, Legacy and Outback vehicles. A weld that was not strong enough can let water get into the inhibitor switch, the switch that tells the car which gear the transmission is in, and the water can make that switch fail. If it does, the reverse lights may not come on and the rearview camera image may not appear. Dealers will replace the switch free of charge.

item.title: Subaru Front Driveshafts May Crack and Break
item.description: On some Subaru Crosstrek, Forester, Impreza, and WRX vehicles, the outer race on the front driveshaft assemblies may develop cracks and break. This can cause a loss of drive power while driving, or cause the vehicle to roll away if it's parked without the parking brake set.

item.title: Subaru Forester Coolant Leak Fire Risk
item.description: Subaru is recalling certain 2024 Forester vehicles because the engine water pipe may have loose attachment bolts, allowing the pipe to lose its seal and leak coolant. Leaking coolant can reach the hot exhaust pipe. Subaru's distributor processing facilities will tighten the water pipe attachment bolts to fix the issue.

item.title: Subaru Driveshaft Bolts May Loosen And Disconnect
item.description: Subaru is recalling certain 2023 Ascent, Impreza, Legacy, and Outback vehicles because of a problem with the driveshaft. The bolts that hold the center support brace for the driveshaft in place may loosen over time. If those bolts loosen too much, the front end of the driveshaft can come apart from the rest of the vehicle. To fix this, dealers will clean the surfaces where the bolts attach and put in new bolts, at no cost to the owner.

item.title: Subaru BRZ and Toyota GR86 rear turn signals fail
item.description: Subaru is recalling certain BRZ vehicles and Toyota GR86 vehicles because the rear turn signals may stop working from time to time. The problem may come and go rather than staying constant. Dealers will replace both rear combination lamp assemblies, the units that hold the rear lights, free of charge. Owner letters were mailed January 8, 2024. Subaru owners and Toyota owners each have their own customer service line for this recall.

item.title: Subaru Crosstrek, Impreza Wiring May Cause Power Loss
item.description: Subaru is recalling certain Crosstrek and Impreza vehicles. On these vehicles, there is not enough clearance between the instrument panel wiring harness and the steering beam bracket. Because of this tight clearance, the wiring harness may come into contact with the bracket and rub against it. This rubbing can wear through the protective insulation around the wires, and once the insulation is worn through, it may lead to a short circuit.

item.title: Subaru Ascent Front Control Arm Ball Joint
item.description: Certain 2023 Subaru Ascent vehicles may have a left or right front lower control arm with a ball joint castle nut that was not tightened properly. This can cause the retention pin to fail and the ball joint to separate from the lower control arm.

item.title: Subaru Impreza Brake Light Switch Adjustment Problem
item.description: The brake light switch on these Imprezas may be adjusted incorrectly, which can cause the brake lights to turn on even when the driver isn't pressing the brake pedal. The same issue can also let the driver start the vehicle and shift the transmission out of Park without pressing the brake pedal.

item.title: Subaru Ascent Tires May Lose Air Suddenly
item.description: Subaru is recalling certain Ascent vehicles equipped with 20-inch wheels. During the wheel mounting process, the internal bead of a tire may have been damaged. A tire with a damaged bead can suddenly lose air pressure while the vehicle is being driven.

item.title: Subaru Crosstrek Hybrid 12-Volt Battery Charging Issue
item.description: On certain Subaru Crosstrek Hybrid vehicles, a wiring terminal that sends low-voltage power to the 12-Volt battery can corrode and break over time. If this happens, the 12-Volt battery is unable to recharge from the vehicle's power system.

item.title: Subaru Solterra Wheels May Come Loose
item.description: Some hub bolts holding the wheels on may not have been tightened correctly. Over time, these bolts can loosen, which can allow a wheel to come loose or detach from the vehicle while it is being driven.

item.title: Subaru WRX Manual Has Wrong High-Beam Instructions
item.description: Subaru is recalling certain WRX vehicles equipped with the Eyesight feature because the owner's manual may contain incorrect instructions for adjusting the sensitivity of the High Beam Assist function. In other words, the printed instructions telling drivers how to change this headlight setting are wrong, which could lead an owner to set it up differently than intended.

item.title: Subaru Ascent Cabin Heater Fire Risk
item.description: A bolt that grounds the wiring for the cabin heater may not have been properly tightened. If it isn't secure, the wiring connection could melt, along with nearby parts. Subaru will replace the bolt, and if needed, the wire and connector, to fix the problem.

item.title: Subaru Impreza and Outback Windshields May Detach
item.description: In some Subaru Impreza and Outback vehicles, the wrong paint clearcoat was used during manufacturing. This can leave the windshield insufficiently bonded, or glued, to the vehicle body. A windshield that is not attached as firmly as it should be does not meet federal safety standards for how windshields must be mounted in a vehicle. This bonding problem happened because of an error made during the painting process at the factory.

item.title: Subaru Impreza reflectors may not reflect enough light
item.description: On these Subaru Impreza cars, the reflectors on the left and right sides, and the low-beam reflector on the left side, may not reflect light well enough. Reflectors are the parts that bounce light back. Because they do not work as they should, these vehicles do not meet the federal safety rule covering lamps, reflective devices and related equipment. To correct it, dealers replace the front headlamp assemblies. Owner notification letters were mailed in November 2023.

item.title: Subaru WRX backup lights and camera may stop working
item.description: Subaru is recalling certain WRX cars. The switch that turns on the backup lights can corrode and stop working. If that happens, the backup lights may not light up and the rearview camera picture may not appear on the screen when the car is shifted into reverse.

item.title: Subaru Legacy and Outback Transmission Chain May Slip
item.description: In some Legacy and Outback vehicles, a programming error in the transmission control unit may let the clutch engage before the drive chain is fully clamped. If the chain isn't properly secured, it can slip and break.

item.title: Subaru Outback Wiring Fault May Cause Engine Stall
item.description: In these vehicles, the wiring that runs to the engine's control computer may have been damaged. This damage can create a loose electrical connection where the wiring plugs into the computer. A loose connection like this can cause the engine to stall while you are driving. Subaru will fix this by replacing the damaged wiring harness along with the engine control computer, so this loose connection can no longer cause the engine to stall.

item.title: Subaru Solterra, Toyota BZ4X Wheel Bolts Loosen
item.description: The bolts that attach the wheel hubs to some Solterra and BZ4X vehicles may loosen over time, even after the vehicle has only been driven a short distance. If a hub bolt loosens enough, the wheel it holds in place can come off the vehicle while it is being driven. Toyota dealers will replace the hub bolts and the wheels on all affected vehicles, free of charge.

item.title: Subaru Ascent, Legacy, Outback Drive Chain Risk
item.description: Subaru is recalling certain Ascent, Legacy, and Outback vehicles because a programming error in the transmission control unit may let the clutch engage before the drive chain is fully clamped. If the chain isn't properly secured, it may slip and break. A broken drive chain causes a loss of drive power, which increases the risk of a crash.

item.title: Subaru Ascent Front Tie Rod May Separate
item.description: Subaru is recalling certain Ascent vehicles because of an incorrect tapered hole in the tie rod housing. This can cause the front tie rod ends to not fit properly, and the tie rods and housings can become deformed during assembly or service if too much torque is applied. As a result, the tie rods may separate from the housing.

item.title: Subaru Impreza Control Arm Weld May Fail
item.description: Subaru is recalling certain Impreza vehicles because the left-front lower control arm weld may fail, allowing the control arm to separate from the crossmember.

item.title: Subaru, Toyota 86 Fuel Pump May Fail
item.description: The low-pressure fuel pump, located inside the fuel tank, may fail on these vehicles. If the pump fails, the engine can stall while the vehicle is being driven. To fix the issue, dealers will replace the low-pressure fuel pump. This repair is free of charge, and it applies to a number of affected Subaru models as well as the Toyota 86.

item.title: Subaru Impreza and Crosstrek Risk Ignition Coil Short Circuit
item.description: Certain Subaru Impreza and Crosstrek vehicles have an engine control module that may keep sending power to the ignition coil even after the engine is turned off. This can cause a short circuit in the ignition coils, which may make the engine stall. Dealers will update the engine control module software, replace the ignition coils, and, if needed, replace the front exhaust pipe.

item.title: Subaru Crosstrek and Forester Loose Suspension Bolts
item.description: On some Subaru Crosstrek and Forester vehicles, the bolts holding the rear stabilizer bracket may loosen and come out. If the bracket isn't held in place, it could shift out of position. A shifted bracket increases the risk of a crash.

item.title: Subaru Impreza, Outback Shifter Cable Nut May Loosen
item.description: On certain 2021 Subaru Outback and Impreza vehicles with a continuously variable transmission, a nut on the shift lever cable may not have been tightened properly. Over time, this nut can loosen, which can cause the cable to lose its grip and the gear selector to stop working correctly. Subaru will notify owners, and dealers will inspect the nut and tighten it if needed.

item.title: Subaru Legacy, Outback Rearview Camera Can Cut Out
item.description: Subaru is recalling certain Legacy and Outback vehicles equipped with the high or mid grade multimedia navigation system. An earlier over-the-air software update did not finish installing correctly, which corrupted some data. As a result, the rearview camera image on the display can shut off intermittently instead of staying on while the driver is backing up.

item.title: Subaru Vehicles May Have Fuel Pump Failure
item.description: Certain Subaru Impreza, Outback, Legacy, and Ascent vehicles have a low pressure fuel pump that may stop working. Dealers will replace the low pressure fuel pump to fix the problem.

item.title: Subaru Crosstrek Rear Seat Belts May Not Lock
item.description: Subaru says the rear seat belts in some Crosstrek vehicles have a dual-mode locking mechanism that senses the belt webbing. That locking mechanism may not lock as intended.

item.title: Subaru Ascent, Crosstrek, Forester Power Loss Risk
item.description: The aluminum Positive Crankcase Ventilation valve in your engine can separate. If it does, the pieces that break off can travel into the engine, causing your vehicle to lose power while you're driving. Subaru will notify owners, and dealers will inspect and replace the valve, free of charge. If the valve has separated and its pieces can't be found, the engine's short block will be replaced instead, free of charge.

item.title: Subaru Ascent Transmission Sensor May Misread Pressure
item.description: Subaru is recalling certain Ascent vehicles because the transmission hydraulic sensor may not measure the transmission fluid pressure accurately. If the sensor reads the pressure as higher than it really is, the actual hydraulic pressure will be reduced. This can cause the transmission drive chain to lose proper tension, resulting in a loss of drive power and an increased risk of a crash.

item.title: Subaru Crosstrek, Impreza Risk of Engine Stall
item.description: Subaru says a computer that controls the engine in some Impreza and Crosstrek vehicles may keep sending power to the ignition coil even after the engine has been turned off. Leaving that power on can lead to a short circuit and a blown fuse. If a short circuit happens while the vehicle is being driven, the vehicle may suddenly stall.

item.title: Subaru Impreza and Crosstrek Engine Valve May Fail
item.description: Some Impreza and Crosstrek vehicles have an engine part that may come apart. If pieces separate, they can get into the engine, and this may cause the engine to suddenly lose power while you are driving.

item.title: Subaru Forester Passenger Airbag May Deactivate
item.description: On certain 2015-2018 Forester vehicles equipped with heated seats, an electrical connection for the front passenger seat's occupant detection system may loosen. If this happens, the front passenger airbag may turn off even though the seat is occupied.
